profile_text.body:
AssistiveWare describes itself as a builder of AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) apps that also shares best practices, working closely with the AAC community to help people communicate. Its site discusses core words, Gestalt Language Processing, and stories about nonspeaking and autistic students, including a film about Ruby Bridges Elementary and the story of Jordyn Zimmerman. A support team member, Lily Konyn, is described as a part-time AAC user who writes about Gestalt Language Processing.

The company's tracked product is Proloquo2Go, listed under Education & Research AI. It uses word prediction and is aimed at students with communication needs and speech-language pathologists. The vendor describes it for users aged 2 and up, while the App Store age rating is 4+. AssistiveWare states that usage data is collected anonymously, and the App Store label lists identifiers and usage data not linked to identity. No school account is needed. The App Store price is $249.99, with an optional Gateway vocabulary at $149.99 as of May 2026.

The held records list no lawsuits and no MCP servers for AssistiveWare.
